variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the Mercedes M270
variants.intro: The M270 engine code (including sub-codes M270.910 and M270.920) is stamped directly onto the engine block, typically near the bell housing or oil filter housing, and is clearly listed on your vehicle's V5C registration document under "Engine Number". **Common Confusion Warning:** Owners frequently confuse the M270 with the closely related M274. While they share the same 2.0-litre turbocharged architecture and internal components, the M270 is mounted transversely for front-wheel-drive compact models (A-Class, B-Class, CLA, GLA), whereas the M274 is mounted longitudinally for rear-wheel-drive platforms (C-Class, E-Class). Fitting an M274 as a replacement for an M270 will result in severe mounting, exhaust, and wiring loom incompatibilities.

relatives.description: The longitudinal predecessor it replaced, which shares similar timing chain and balance shaft vulnerabilities but differs entirely in mounting orientation and accessory layout.

The newer modular successor that dropped the transverse 2.0L layout in favour of a lighter 1.3L/1.4L configuration for compact models, though some late M270 applications overlapped with early M282 introductions.

The longitudinal twin of this engine; owners of rear-wheel-drive C-Class or E-Class models with similar symptoms should look here instead, as the M274 is not a direct physical swap for the transverse M270.

items.question: What is the most common failure with the Mercedes M270 engine?
items.answer: The most documented failure pattern for the M270 is timing chain stretch and tensioner wear, particularly in early production units, leading to cold-start rattling and potential check engine lights. Additionally, camshaft adjuster oil leaks and turbo wastegate rattles are common secondary issues that can lead to oil starvation or boost faults if ignored.
items.cta: Get quotes for a rebuilt M270 with these known weaknesses addressed.

items.question: Which Mercedes models use the M270 engine?
items.answer: The M270 is fitted to Mercedes-Benz front-wheel-drive compact models from 2012 to 2018, including the A-Class (W176), B-Class (W246), CLA (C117/X117), and GLA (X156). It powers badges ranging from the A200 and A250 to the GLA200 and GLA250, and you should always verify your exact fitment via registration lookup.
items.cta: Confirm your exact M270 fitment before requesting a quote.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned Mercedes M270 engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned Mercedes M270 is strongly recommended over a used unit due to the known timing chain stretch and oil leak risks. Used units carry a high risk of inheriting the same latent defects unless accompanied by stamped proof of preventative chain replacement, whereas reconditioned units include updated chain kits, tensioners, and revised seals, providing a reliable long-term solution.
items.cta: View our reconditioned Mercedes M270 engine options with 12-month warranties.

items.question: How do I know if my car has the M270 and not the M274?
items.answer: The M270 engine code (including sub-codes M270.910 and M270.920) is stamped on the engine block near the bell housing or oil filter housing and is listed on your V5C registration document. It is commonly confused with the M274, but the M270 is mounted transversely for front-wheel-drive models, meaning fitting an M274 will result in severe mounting, exhaust, and wiring loom incompatibilities.
